requirements.original: The restrictions in clause 16.1.2 apply.
requirements.canonical: Each restriction of clause 16.1.2 IS applicable to `decvalue_unichar`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.4 -- The restrictions in clause 16.1.2 apply.

requirements.original: encvalue_o(in template (value) any inpar, in universal charstring encoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "", out integer bit_length) return octetstring
requirements.canonical: The `encvalue_o` predefined function has the signature encvalue_o(in template (value) any inpar, in universal charstring encoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "", out integer bit_length) return octetstring.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.5 -- encvalue_o(in template (value) any inpar, in universal charstring encoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "", out integer bit_length) return octetstring

requirements.original: The encvalue_o function encodes a value or template into an octetstring.
requirements.canonical: The `encvalue_o` function IS the predefined function that encodes a value or template into an octetstring.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.5 -- The encvalue_o function encodes a value or template into an octetstring.

requirements.original: When the actual parameter that is passed to inpar is a template, it shall resolve to a specific value (the same restrictions apply as for the argument of the send statement).
requirements.canonical: When the actual parameter passed to the `inpar` formal parameter of `encvalue_o` is a template, the template SHALL resolve to a specific value.
requirements.condition: the actual parameter passed to inpar is a template

ambiguity.issue: The standard calls `send` an operation (clause 22.2.1); 'send statement' deviates from that term.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.5 -- When the actual parameter that is passed to inpar is a template, it shall resolve to a specific value (the same restrictions apply as for the argument of the send statement).

requirements.original: When the actual parameter that is passed to inpar is a template, it shall resolve to a specific value (the same restrictions apply as for the argument of the send statement).
requirements.canonical: The actual parameter passed to the `inpar` formal parameter of `encvalue_o` IS subject to the same restrictions as the argument of the `send` operation.

ambiguity.issue: The standard calls `send` an operation (clause 22.2.1); 'send statement' deviates from that term.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.5 -- When the actual parameter that is passed to inpar is a template, it shall resolve to a specific value (the same restrictions apply as for the argument of the send statement).

requirements.original: The returned octetstring represents the encoded value of inpar, however, the TTCN-3 test system need not make any check on its correctness.
requirements.canonical: The octetstring returned by `encvalue_o` IS the encoded value of `inpar`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.5 -- The returned octetstring represents the encoded value of inpar, however, the TTCN-3 test system need not make any check on its correctness.

requirements.original: In case the encoded message is not octet-based and has a bit length not divisible by 8, the encoded message will be left-aligned in the returned octetstring and the least significant (8 - (bit length mod 8)) bits in the least significant octet will be 0.
requirements.canonical: If the encoded message is not octet-based and its bit length is not divisible by 8, the encoded message IS left-aligned in the octetstring returned by `encvalue_o`.
requirements.condition: the encoded message is not octet-based and its bit length is not divisible by 8
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.5 -- In case the encoded message is not octet-based and has a bit length not divisible by 8, the encoded message will be left-aligned in the returned octetstring and the least significant (8 - (bit length mod 8)) bits in the least significant octet will be 0.

requirements.original: In case the encoded message is not octet-based and has a bit length not divisible by 8, the encoded message will be left-aligned in the returned octetstring and the least significant (8 - (bit length mod 8)) bits in the least significant octet will be 0.
requirements.canonical: If the encoded message is not octet-based and its bit length is not divisible by 8, each of the least significant (8 - (bit length mod 8)) bits of the least significant octet returned by `encvalue_o` IS 0.
requirements.condition: the encoded message is not octet-based and its bit length is not divisible by 8
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.5 -- In case the encoded message is not octet-based and has a bit length not divisible by 8, the encoded message will be left-aligned in the returned octetstring and the least significant (8 - (bit length mod 8)) bits in the least significant octet will be 0.

requirements.original: The bit length can be assigned to a variable by usage of the formal out parameter bit_length.
requirements.canonical: The bit length of the encoded message CAN be assigned to a variable through the `out` formal parameter `bit_length` of `encvalue_o`.

readings: The `bit_length` out parameter of `encvalue_o` is mandatory and always receives the bit length of the encoded message.
The `bit_length` out parameter of `encvalue_o` is optional and may be skipped by the caller when the bit length is not needed.
ambiguity.issue: 'can be assigned' and the position of `bit_length` after defaulted parameters leave open whether the actual parameter may be omitted; out parameters have no default value, so the mandatory reading was chosen.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.5 -- The bit length can be assigned to a variable by usage of the formal out parameter bit_length.

requirements.original: The optional dynamic_encoding parameter is used for dynamic selection of encode attribute of the inpar value for this single encvalue_o call.
requirements.canonical: The optional `dynamic_encoding` parameter of `encvalue_o` IS used for dynamic selection of the encode attribute of the `inpar` value for this single `encvalue_o` call.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.5 -- The optional dynamic_encoding parameter is used for dynamic selection of encode attribute of the inpar value for this single encvalue_o call.

requirements.original: The rules for dynamic selection of the encode attribute are described in clause 27.9.
requirements.canonical: The dynamic selection of the encode attribute in a call of `encvalue_o` IS governed by the rules of clause 27.9.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.5 -- The rules for dynamic selection of the encode attribute are described in clause 27.9.

requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:
requirements.canonical: Each general error cause of clause 16.1.2 IS applicable to a call of `encvalue_o`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.5 -- In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are: Encoding fails due to a runtime system problem (i.e. no encoding function exists for the actual type of inpar).
requirements.canonical: A call of `encvalue_o` SHALL cause an error when encoding fails due to a runtime system problem, i.e. when no encoding function exists for the actual type of `inpar`.
requirements.condition: no encoding function exists for the actual type of inpar
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.5 -- In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are: Encoding fails due to a runtime system problem (i.e. no encoding function exists for the actual type of inpar).

requirements.original: decvalue_o(inout octetstring encoded_value, out any decoded_value, in universal charstring decoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return integer
requirements.canonical: The `decvalue_o` predefined function has the signature decvalue_o(inout octetstring encoded_value, out any decoded_value, in universal charstring decoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return integer.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.6 -- decvalue_o(inout octetstring encoded_value, out any decoded_value, in universal charstring decoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return integer

requirements.original: The decvalue_o function decodes an octetstring into a value.
requirements.canonical: The `decvalue_o` function IS the predefined function that decodes an octetstring into a value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.6 -- The decvalue_o function decodes an octetstring into a value.

requirements.original: The optional dynamic_encoding parameter is used for dynamic selection of encode attribute of the decoded_value parameter for this single decvalue_o call.
requirements.canonical: The optional `dynamic_encoding` parameter of `decvalue_o` IS used for dynamic selection of the encode attribute of the `decoded_value` parameter for this single `decvalue_o` call.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.6 -- The optional dynamic_encoding parameter is used for dynamic selection of encode attribute of the decoded_value parameter for this single decvalue_o call.

requirements.original: The rules for dynamic selection of the encode attribute are described in clause 27.9.
requirements.canonical: The dynamic selection of the encode attribute in a call of `decvalue_o` IS governed by the rules of clause 27.9.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.6 -- The rules for dynamic selection of the encode attribute are described in clause 27.9.

requirements.original: If the decoding was successful, then the used octets are removed from the parameter encoded_value, the rest is returned (in the parameter encoded_value), and the decoded value is returned in the parameter decoded_value.
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue_o` is successful, the part of `encoded_value` consumed by decoding (the used octets) IS removed from the `encoded_value` parameter.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.6 -- If the decoding was successful, then the used octets are removed from the parameter encoded_value, the rest is returned (in the parameter encoded_value), and the decoded value is returned in the parameter decoded_value.

requirements.original: If the decoding was successful, then the used octets are removed from the parameter encoded_value, the rest is returned (in the parameter encoded_value), and the decoded value is returned in the parameter decoded_value.
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue_o` is successful, the remaining undecoded part of the input IS returned in the `encoded_value` parameter.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.6 -- If the decoding was successful, then the used octets are removed from the parameter encoded_value, the rest is returned (in the parameter encoded_value), and the decoded value is returned in the parameter decoded_value.

requirements.original: If the decoding was successful, then the used octets are removed from the parameter encoded_value, the rest is returned (in the parameter encoded_value), and the decoded value is returned in the parameter decoded_value.
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue_o` is successful, the decoded value IS returned in the `decoded_value` parameter.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.6 -- If the decoding was successful, then the used octets are removed from the parameter encoded_value, the rest is returned (in the parameter encoded_value), and the decoded value is returned in the parameter decoded_value.

requirements.original: If the decoding was unsuccessful, the actual parameters for encoded_value and decoded_value are not changed.
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue_o` is unsuccessful, the value of each of the actual parameters for `encoded_value` and `decoded_value` IS NOT changed.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.6 -- If the decoding was unsuccessful, the actual parameters for encoded_value and decoded_value are not changed.

requirements.original: The function shall return an integer value to indicate success or failure of the decoding below:
requirements.canonical: The `decvalue_o` function SHALL return an integer value indicating success or failure of the decoding.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.6 -- The function shall return an integer value to indicate success or failure of the decoding below:

requirements.original: The return value 0 indicates that decoding was successful.
requirements.canonical: The return value 0 of `decvalue_o` IS the indication that decoding was successful.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.6 -- The return value 0 indicates that decoding was successful.

requirements.original: The return value 1 indicates an unspecified cause of decoding failure.
requirements.canonical: The return value 1 of `decvalue_o` IS the indication of an unspecified cause of decoding failure.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.6 -- The return value 1 indicates an unspecified cause of decoding failure.

requirements.original: This value is also returned if the encoded_value parameter contains an unitialized value.
requirements.canonical: If the `encoded_value` actual parameter of `decvalue_o` contains an uninitialized value, `decvalue_o` SHALL return 1.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.6 -- This value is also returned if the encoded_value parameter contains an unitialized value.

requirements.original: The return value 2 indicates that decoding could not be completed as encoded_value did not contain enough octets.
requirements.canonical: The return value 2 of `decvalue_o` IS the indication that decoding could not be completed because `encoded_value` did not contain enough octets.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.6 -- The return value 2 indicates that decoding could not be completed as encoded_value did not contain enough octets.

requirements.original: The restrictions in clause 16.1.2 apply.
requirements.canonical: Each restriction of clause 16.1.2 IS applicable to `decvalue_o`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.6 -- The restrictions in clause 16.1.2 apply.

requirements.original: get_stringencoding(in octetstring encoded_value) return charstring
requirements.canonical: The `get_stringencoding` predefined function has the signature get_stringencoding(in octetstring encoded_value) return charstring.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.7 -- get_stringencoding(in octetstring encoded_value) return charstring

requirements.original: The get_stringencoding function analyses the encoded_value and returns the UCS encoding scheme according to clause 10 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2] (see also clause 27.5 of the present document).
requirements.canonical: The `get_stringencoding` function IS the predefined function that analyses `encoded_value` and returns its UCS encoding scheme according to clause 10 of ISO/IEC 10646.

examples.text:
match ( get_stringencoding('6869C3BA7A'O),charstring:"UTF-8") // true
  //(the octetstring contains the UTF-8 encoding of the character sequence "hiúz")

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.7 -- The get_stringencoding function analyses the encoded_value and returns the UCS encoding scheme according to clause 10 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2] (see also clause 27.5 of the present document).

requirements.original: The identified encoding scheme, or the value "<unknown>", if the type of encoding cannot be determined unanimously, shall be returned as a character string.
requirements.canonical: The `get_stringencoding` function SHALL return the identified UCS encoding scheme of `encoded_value` as a charstring.
requirements.condition: the encoding scheme can be determined unambiguously

examples.text:
match ( get_stringencoding('6869C3BA7A'O),charstring:"UTF-8") // true
  //(the octetstring contains the UTF-8 encoding of the character sequence "hiúz")

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.7 -- The identified encoding scheme, or the value "<unknown>", if the type of encoding cannot be determined unanimously, shall be returned as a character string.

requirements.original: The identified encoding scheme, or the value "<unknown>", if the type of encoding cannot be determined unanimously, shall be returned as a character string.
requirements.canonical: If the encoding scheme of `encoded_value` cannot be determined unambiguously, `get_stringencoding` SHALL return the charstring "<unknown>".
requirements.condition: the encoding scheme cannot be determined unambiguously
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.7 -- The identified encoding scheme, or the value "<unknown>", if the type of encoding cannot be determined unanimously, shall be returned as a character string.

requirements.original: remove_bom(in octetstring encoded_value) return octetstring
requirements.canonical: The `remove_bom` predefined function has the signature remove_bom(in octetstring encoded_value) return octetstring.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.8 -- remove_bom(in octetstring encoded_value) return octetstring

requirements.original: The remove_bom function removes the optional FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE sequence that may be present at the beginning of a stream of serialized (encoded) universal character strings to indicate the order of the octets within the encoding form, as defined in clause 10 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].
requirements.canonical: The `remove_bom` function IS the predefined function that removes the optional FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE sequence (byte order mark) from the beginning of `encoded_value`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.8 -- The remove_bom function removes the optional FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE sequence that may be present at the beginning of a stream of serialized (encoded) universal character strings to indicate the order of the octets within the encoding form, as defined in clause 10 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.original: If no FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE sequence present in the encoded_value parameter, the function shall return the value of the parameter without change.
requirements.canonical: If `encoded_value` contains no FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE sequence, `remove_bom` SHALL return the value of `encoded_value` unchanged.
requirements.condition: encoded_value contains no FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE sequence
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.8 -- If no FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE sequence present in the encoded_value parameter, the function shall return the value of the parameter without change.

requirements.original: rnd([in float seed]) return float
requirements.canonical: The `rnd` function has the signature `rnd([in float seed]) return float`, with an optional `in` formal parameter `seed` of type `float` and a return value of type `float`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.1 -- rnd([in float seed]) return float

requirements.original: The rnd function returns a (pseudo) random number less than 1 but greater or equal to 0.
requirements.canonical: The `rnd` function returns a (pseudo) random `float` value that is greater than or equal to 0 and less than 1.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.1 -- The rnd function returns a (pseudo) random number less than 1 but greater or equal to 0.

requirements.original: The random number generator is initialized per test component and for the control part by means of an optional seed value (a numerical float value).
requirements.canonical: The random number generator used by `rnd` IS initialized separately per test component and per module control function.

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.1 -- The random number generator is initialized per test component and for the control part by means of an optional seed value (a numerical float value).

requirements.original: The random number generator is initialized per test component and for the control part by means of an optional seed value (a numerical float value).
requirements.canonical: The random number generator of `rnd` MAY be initialized by passing an optional seed value of type `float` as actual parameter of `rnd`.

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.1 -- The random number generator is initialized per test component and for the control part by means of an optional seed value (a numerical float value).

requirements.original: If no new seed is provided, the last generated number will be used as seed for the next random number.
requirements.canonical: If `rnd` is called without a new seed value, the last random number generated by `rnd` IS used as seed for the next random number.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether this is an observable rule (re-seeding with the last returned value) or an informal description of the generator state continuing; the first reading was chosen as it is the literal one.
readings: A call `rnd()` IS equivalent to `rnd(r)`, where r is the last value returned by `rnd` in the same test component or module control function.
A call `rnd()` IS the continuation of the current pseudo random sequence, with the generator-internal state acting as seed; the returned value need not equal `rnd(r)`.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.1 -- If no new seed is provided, the last generated number will be used as seed for the next random number.

requirements.original: Each time the rnd function is initialized with the same seed value, it shall repeat the same sequence of random numbers.
requirements.canonical: Each time `rnd` is initialized with the same seed value, `rnd` SHALL repeat the same sequence of random numbers.
requirements.condition: rnd is initialized with the same seed value
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.1 -- Each time the rnd function is initialized with the same seed value, it shall repeat the same sequence of random numbers.

requirements.original: NOTE: For the purpose of keeping parallel testing deterministic, each test component, as well as the control part has its own random seed.
requirements.canonical: Each test component and the module control function has its own random seed, to keep parallel testing deterministic.

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.1 -- NOTE: For the purpose of keeping parallel testing deterministic, each test component, as well as the control part has its own random seed.

requirements.original: Thus, the rnd function will always use the seed of the component or control part which calls it.
requirements.canonical: The `rnd` function always uses the seed of the test component or module control function that calls it.

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.1 -- Thus, the rnd function will always use the seed of the component or control part which calls it.

requirements.original: To produce a random integers in a given range, the following formula can be used: float2int(int2float(upperbound - lowerbound +1)*rnd()) + lowerbound
requirements.canonical: A random integer in the range lowerbound..upperbound CAN be produced with the expression `float2int(int2float(upperbound - lowerbound + 1) * rnd()) + lowerbound`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.1 -- To produce a random integers in a given range, the following formula can be used: float2int(int2float(upperbound - lowerbound +1)*rnd()) + lowerbound

requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of predefined functions defined in clause 16.1.2 apply to `rnd`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.1 -- In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.original: seed is infinity, -infinity or not_a_number.
requirements.canonical: If the seed actual parameter of `rnd` is `infinity`, `-infinity` or `not_a_number`, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.1 -- seed is infinity, -infinity or not_a_number.
